title: Campaigns OS Release Ledger v1
description: The append-only, agent-relevant release ledger. One ordered entry per accepted release or reviewed amendment; one change item per agent-relevant semantic change. An entry deliberately carries NO commit identifier: an entry cannot name the commit that contains it without being rewritten after the fact, so a consumer derives the introducing commit from Git history at the immutable target OID instead. Historical entries are never rewritten; a correction ships as a new amendment entry. A consumer that recognizes v1 accepts and preserves unknown additive properties without interpreting them; required fields, known types, and safety-critical enums remain strict.

entries.description: Ordered oldest to newest. sequence is strictly increasing by 1 from 1, and date is non-decreasing.

id.description: Stable, immutable entry identity. Never reused, never renumbered.

sequence.description: Position in the append-only order. Strictly increasing by 1.

date.description: The acceptance date. Non-decreasing across entries.

kind.description: release: a change to the repository. amendment: a reviewed correction to an earlier entry's meaning. An amendment is the ONLY entry kind permitted to carry change items that map to no changed path in its own commit range.

amends.description: Required on kind: amendment; forbidden on kind: release. The earlier entry this corrects. The earlier entry's bytes are not touched.

amendment_reason.description: Required on kind: amendment. Why the earlier entry was wrong or incomplete.

surface_version.description: The supported-surface version this entry accompanies, or null for a same-surface change. A surface_version change owes exactly one entry with that version.

changelog_section.description: The exact CHANGELOG.md section identifier this entry links to, as it appears in the heading '## [<id>] - <date>'. A surface release uses the bare version. A same-surface change uses '<current-version>+agent.<n>', which sorts at the same version and never claims a release that did not happen. Exactly one section may carry a given identifier.

changelog_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 bytes of the linked changelog section body, heading line included, trailing whitespace trimmed. A body edit without a hash update fails the correspondence gate.

agent_impact.description: What a downstream agent must do differently, in plain language. 'None' is a valid assertion but must be written, not omitted.

compatibility.description: compatible: no consumer change. additive: new surface a consumer may adopt. breaking: an existing consumer stops working without action.

migration.description: The exact operator or consumer action, or the literal string 'none'. A breaking entry may not say 'none'.

changes.description: One item per agent-relevant semantic change. Change identity is (class, path, surface_entry) and must be unique within this entry; later releases may record a new change to the same path.

entry_sha256.description: SHA-256 over the canonical JSON of this entry with entry_sha256 removed. Makes an in-place edit of a historical entry detectable even in a squashed history.

class.description: The semantic class, defined once in contracts/agent-relevant-change-policy.v1.json. The enum here is checked against that file.

path.description: The repository-relative path this change covers, or null when the class has no single path (a CLI flag, for example). A non-null path must classify to this item's class under the change policy.

surface_entry.description: The contracts/supported-surface.json entry this change affects (a hashed path, a named path, a cli_commands name, a package_exports subpath, or a bin name), or null when the change touches no supported entry.

summary.description: One sentence naming what changed, written for a consumer, not for the author.
